title: CUDA library chain debug: heap & driver ABI breadcrumbs
content:
Quick scratchpad — trying to capture commands, snippets and hypotheses for a recurring crash we saw on a few Dedicated nodes. Not formal, mostly breadcrumbs for follow-ups.

Problem summary:
- Symptoms: intermittent CUDA OOMs inside containerized PyTorch jobs, often during warmup or eval. Sometimes processes crash with import/runtime errors before any big allocations. Host driver had recently been updated to 535.x.
- Machine: g5.2x (A100-ish equivalent) — single GPU per container.
- Container base: ubuntu:22.04 image built with CUDA runtime libs via apt and conda env for python.

Timeline / attempts:
2025-01-08 09:12 — first repro (local dev node)
- docker run --gpus=all -it --rm --name repro --entrypoint=/bin/bash repro-image
- inside: python -c "import torch; print(torch.__version__); print(torch.version.cuda); torch.zeros(1024,1024,1024, device='cuda')"
- error: RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.00 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 39.00 GiB already allocated)
  - But nvtop/nvidia-smi showed nothing allocated before running script (process list empty).

2025-01-09 11:40 — container import fails in some jobs
- python startup stack: ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
  - ldd $(python -c "import torch; import os, sys; print(torch._C.__file__)" ) shows missing libs pointing to /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.0
- However inside container /usr/local/cuda is present; libcudart* are present but symlink versions mismatch (libcudart.so -> libcudart.so.11.8) while torch expects 11.0 SONAME.

Commands used for inspection:
- nvidia-smi
  NVIDIA-SMI 535.86.10 Driver Version: 535.86.10 CUDA Version: 12.1
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
- ls -l /usr/local/cuda/lib64 | grep cudart
  lrwxrwxrwx 1 root root 20 Jan 1 2024 libcudart.so -> libcudart.so.11.8.74
- ldd $(python -c "import torch; print(torch._C.__file__)") | grep cudart || true
- ldconfig -p | grep libcudart
- strings /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so.11.8 | head -n 5

Hypothesis A: SONAME mismatch between torch wheel and system CUDA libs
- Some PyTorch builds are linked to a specific SONAME (libcudart.so.11.0) while host has newer 11.x patch with SONAME 11.8 — but usually the SONAME major is 11 so should be compatible. However the import error suggests exact filename missing.
- Quick workaround attempted: create a symlink libcudart.so.11.0 -> libcudart.so.11.8 (temporary) inside container; import succeeds sometimes, but then new errors appear at runtime (segfaults inside cublas).

Hypothesis B: Mixed runtime / driver compatibility (CUDA runtime version vs driver)
- Host driver reports support up to CUDA 12.1, container runtime libs are 11.x — that normally is fine (driver backward compatible). But observed message in some logs: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" when running binary built against 12.x inside container. Possibly one of the model eval tasks is picking up a different libcuda from host path.

Hypothesis C: LD_LIBRARY_PATH / container mount inconsistency leading to partial lib chain (libcudart ok but cuBLAS/cuFFT missing)
- Some containers mount /usr/local/cuda from host as a volume at runtime in our deploys. If the host supplied /usr/local/cuda is from a different driver/toolkit install, it can mismatch.

Interesting logs/tail snippets:
- dmesg | tail after crash:
  [12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31, PID=2345, Name: python3, GPU=00000000:01:00.0, Ch 00000040, Class 0x0000b, Reason: Invalid PTX or unsupported relocs
  [12345.679002] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
- kernel logs show TDR-like resets or GPU scheduling errors preceding OOMs for some runs.

Repro attempts and results:
- Create minimal repro that just imports torch and allocates smaller tensors (to isolate warmup): sometimes allocation fails at 16 MiB allocation step with OOM message similar to above.
- Running the same container image on a different host (driver 520.x) did NOT reproduce the segfaults, only the missing-soname import error (fixed with symlink).
- Running with --env LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 suppressed some import errors but caused different symbol lookup failures (undefined symbol: cuInit) — indicates mixing of driver lib with different symbol versions.

Commands that changed behavior:
- docker run ... --volume /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/:/host-libs:ro ... and then inside container export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host-libs:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH 
  -> sometimes fixes import but unstable.
- ldd on /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 shows NEEDED libs to libnvidia-ml.so, etc.

Experiment notes (what I tried, outcome):
- Rebuild image with conda pytorch pinned to cudatoolkit=11.8 instead of expecting system CUDA: reduced import errors, still intermittent OOMs.
- Force embedding allocator to use max_split_size_mb=128 (torch.cuda.set_per_process_memory_fraction) — decreased incidence but not eliminated.
- Upgraded driver on one host from 535.x -> 535.99 (minor) — no change.
- Rolled back driver to 520.x on a repro machine — seemed more stable; can't tell if due to driver or different /usr/local/cuda content on that host.

Key hypotheses to test next:
1) Confirm whether /usr/local/cuda is bind-mounted from host in prod deploys (ask infra) — if yes, that explains cross-host variability.
2) Build fully self-contained image that bundles cuda runtime libs (cudatoolkit 11.8 via conda) and ensure no host /usr/local/cuda mounts; run across hosts to see if behavior is consistent.
3) Use nvidia-container-cli to inspect which libs are actually mapped into container at runtime (nvidia-container-cli -k -v list) and snapshot file map for failing run.
4) Reproduce with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and run under gdb to get precise crash backtrace for segfaults.

Quick commands to run for reproducibility capture (add to job wrapper):
- env | grep CUDA
- ldd $(python -c "import torch, sys; print(torch._C.__file__)") || true
- ldconfig -p | grep cuda || true
- nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/nvidia-smi-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).xml
- nvidia-container-cli -k -v list --pid $PID > /tmp/nvidia-files.$PID

Notes / reminders:
- Creating naive symlinks can mask the real ABI incompatibility and produce subtle corruption (seen cublas miscomputations).
- Prefer shipping a container with consistent cudatoolkit & torch wheel that match, and avoid mounting host /usr/local/cuda. For Dedicated we sometimes mount host toolkits to save space — that looks risky here.

Raw error excerpts collected:
- "ImportError: libcudart.so.11.0: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory"
- "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.02 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity)"
- dmesg: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 31"
- python segfault backtrace: "SIGSEGV at 0x7f8c5f000000 in libcudart.so.11.8"

Follow-ups for infra / SRE:
- Confirm whether our deployment templates mount host /usr/local/cuda by default (templates: infra/images/dedicated-runtime.json?)
- Add nvidia-container-cli capture to failing job wrapper to persist file mapping for post-mortem.
- Consider a short pilot to run critical jobs with a fully self-contained image pinned to cudatoolkit=11.8 and no host mounts; compare failure rate for 24h.

If I get time: instrument a tiny C extension that prints cudaDriverGetVersion and cudaRuntimeGetVersion to validate runtime vs driver inside container in the failing environment.

End of notes.

-- Ethan
